entries.title: Does a railroad conductor have the same job as the driver?
entries.answer: A railroad conductor helps coordinate the work of a train and its crew. A locomotive engineer is the person who operates the engine and controls the train’s movement. On a passenger train, a conductor can have responsibilities connected to riders and the trip. On a freight train the work may include following information about which cars need to travel or be set out. A crew needs to share information so everybody is working from the same plan.
facts: Locomotive engineer is a railroad job name for someone who drives a train.

questions.text: How do signals help railroad crews understand what is ahead?
What do freight trains carry?
How does a train move from one track onto another?

entries.title: How a magnetic compass points a direction
entries.answer: A compass has a magnetic needle that can turn with little friction. Earth has a magnetic field that gives the needle a direction. The end marked north generally points close to geographic north in many places, but the exact direction depends on where you stand. Maps can give a correction for this difference. A magnet or a piece of iron held nearby can also pull the needle away from where it would otherwise point.
facts: The angle between local compass north and geographic north is called magnetic declination.

questions.text: How can two magnets change each other’s direction?
How do we describe a place’s position measured north or south?
What icy moon also makes a magnetic field of its own?

entries.title: How can a printer use the same letters in different books?
entries.answer: Movable type uses small pieces with letters or other signs on their faces. A printer sets the pieces in a frame to make lines of writing, puts ink on them, and presses them against paper. After making enough copies, the printer can take the pieces apart and arrange them to make another page. In Europe, Gutenberg’s workshop used a system like this in the 1400s. People in East Asia had made books with movable type earlier.
facts: The Gutenberg Bible was printed in Europe around 1455.

questions.text: How did people make the sheets on which printers printed?
How is printing a whole design from one block different?
How did books and printing affect life in Song cities?

entries.title: How can six keys make a raised braille character?
entries.answer: A basic braille cell has room for six raised dots in two columns. A braille writer has one dot key for each position. To make a character, the writer presses the needed keys together. The machine presses raised bumps into thick paper at those spots. After feeling the dots, a reader can recognize the pattern. Holding two keys at the same time makes a single character containing two raised dots in the right places.
facts: A computer can also take braille input from six keys set up for that purpose.

questions.text: How do readers recognize braille by touch?
How does a typewriter leave marks for ink letters instead?
How can a program share text without needing printed pages?

entries.title: How could a typewriter make one printed letter at a time?
entries.answer: In a common mechanical typewriter, each key moves a piece of metal with a raised letter or number at its end. When it hits an inked ribbon, the ribbon leaves that character on the paper. The machine moves the paper holder a little to make room for the next letter. When the writer reaches the end of a line, moving the holder back brings a fresh line into place.
facts: An early successful typewriter already used the QWERTY order still found on many computer keyboards.

questions.text: How did people print a page using separate pieces for letters?
How does a very different writing tool put ink on paper?
How can a machine make raised dots on a page?

entries.title: How could an early telephone carry a voice down a wire?
entries.answer: When someone speaks, waves in the air make thin parts of a telephone shake. In an early wired telephone, a moving part changed an electrical signal that traveled down a wire. At the other end, the changing signal made a different thin part shake. Its motion pushed the nearby air and a listener could hear something like the original voice. Unlike in a telegraph, each person could speak right away without knowing a code.
facts: Alexander Graham Bell patented an early telephone in 1876.

questions.text: How did a telegraph send words without sending a voice?
How could someone choose whose phone to call?
How can sound make an electrical signal inside a microphone?

entries.title: How did a roll of film change what a camera could do?
entries.answer: A roll of photographic film can hold several pictures along the same strip. Light enters the camera and leaves an image on one part of the film. Turning a handle moves that part away so a clean stretch is ready for another picture. In 1888, the first Kodak camera came with film already loaded. Its owner could take pictures and send the camera away to have the pictures made visible and printed.
facts: The original Kodak could take up to 100 pictures on a roll.

questions.text: What did a much earlier photographer use instead of roll film?
What happens when a camera takes many pictures in quick order?
How do modern pictures stay on a computer without a strip of film?

entries.title: How did a switchboard connect two people on the telephone?
entries.answer: At an early telephone exchange, lines from many homes and businesses reached one switchboard. When one person wanted to call another, an operator found both lines. The operator plugged in cords to join the two lines for that call. Once it was over, the cords could be used to connect different people. Later equipment handled many of these steps automatically, so callers could dial a number without asking for an operator first.
facts: A switchboard could connect different pairs of calls at the same time.

questions.text: How did the first wired telephones carry voices?
How does a network device choose where computer data should go?
What earlier wires carried messages far beyond one town?

entries.title: How did an early phonograph save and play back a voice?
entries.answer: In an early phonograph, a sound made a thin part move back and forth. It carried a small point that made marks on foil wrapped around a turning cylinder. During playback, a point followed the marks and made a thin part move again. That movement made nearby air vibrate so someone could hear a rough copy of the sound that had been saved.
facts: Thomas Edison demonstrated a tinfoil phonograph in the 1870s.

questions.text: How can a microphone turn a voice into an electric signal?
How does a loudspeaker make a recorded voice heard?
How can many sound waves reach you after you stop speaking?

entries.title: How did people turn plant material into paper?
entries.answer: To make many kinds of paper, people separate plant material into tiny strands, mix them with water, and lift a thin layer on a screen. As the water drains, the strands stay in a mat. Pressing and drying make the mat into a sheet. People in China used paper early in its history, and workshops improved ways of making it over time. The idea of making light sheets from wet strands gave writers another choice besides heavier surfaces such as stone or clay.
facts: Archaeological finds show that some paper existed in China before the official Cai Lun reported improvements in 105 CE.

questions.text: How did scribes use clay before paper was widely available?
How did printers later make many copies on paper?
What is one way a carved block can leave a picture on a page?

entries.title: How did the electric telegraph send words down a wire?
entries.answer: People used an electric telegraph to send messages between places joined by a wire. At one end, an operator pressed a key to turn the signal on and off. At the other end, a machine made marks or sounds at matching times. Short and long signals could stand for letters in a system called Morse code. An operator who knew the code could turn those marks or sounds back into words.
facts: An early U.S. telegraph line carried a message from Washington to Baltimore in 1844.

questions.text: How can a switch open or close a path for electricity?
How did a message cross the Atlantic by wire?
How did a later device send a voice instead of signals for letters?

entries.title: How do masonry workers build with blocks, brick, or stone?
entries.answer: Masonry workers build with pieces such as brick, stone, and concrete blocks. A bricklayer follows a plan and uses tools to keep each row even and the wall upright. Mortar can fill gaps and join the bricks. Workers plan for openings, since bricks above a door or window cannot rest on empty space. Masonry work can also include repairing old walls or replacing damaged parts.
facts: A row of bricks or blocks in a wall is called a course.

questions.text: What is the material often placed between bricks?
Why do rows of bricks often begin in different places?
How do the top and bottom of a loaded beam feel different forces?

entries.title: How do people learn a traditional craft?
entries.answer: Someone learning a traditional craft can watch a person who already knows the work, try a step, and ask what to change. A basket maker might show a learner which plants bend without snapping. A potter can feel when clay is ready to shape and help others learn that feeling. Tools and finished objects can give clues, but practice and time with people who know the craft can keep the skills going.
facts: A skill can stay part of a tradition even when people use it to make new designs.

questions.text: What kinds of skills can be a living tradition?
How can people pass on words and stories as well as hand skills?
What work helps museums preserve objects?

entries.title: How does a can opener run its little cutting wheel around a can?
entries.answer: A hand can opener can have two small wheels near each other. The rough wheel grips the rim of the can. The sharp wheel reaches the part it will cut. Turning the handle moves the rough wheel, which helps feed the can past the sharp one. The cut follows the rim as the can moves. Designs differ in where they cut and what edge they leave.
facts: On many hand openers, squeezing two handles brings the wheels together around the rim.

questions.text: How does a long handle give a wrench more turning effect?
What makes a little sharp edge split paper or tape?
How does a lever lift one side of a bottle cap?

entries.title: How does a city bus driver keep track of a route?
entries.answer: A public bus driver carries people along a route with set stops. The driver watches the road and the people arriving at each stop, and works to keep the bus close to its schedule. When something happens along the route, such as a street closing, the driver may get new instructions from people coordinating the service. The same route can be quiet at one hour and full at another.
facts: Some public bus drivers operate buses on routes that connect with trains or with other bus routes.

questions.text: Why can one bus route serve many riders at shared stops?
What is a school bus driver’s route like?
How can a train carry many people across a city?

entries.title: How does a classroom aide help a teacher?
entries.answer: A classroom aide, or teacher assistant, helps pupils practice and helps the teacher run the room. During a lesson, an aide might work with a small group that needs more time with the same idea. At another time, the aide may get materials ready for a class activity. The teacher and aide work together, so the help in the room fits what the class is studying. The exact tasks can change from class to class.
facts: A teacher assistant may help one pupil, a small group, or a whole class at different times.

questions.text: How does a teacher decide which explanation to try next?
Who helps pupils get between school and an assigned stop?
Who helps keep the room ready to use?

entries.title: How does a hinge let a door turn without falling away?
entries.answer: One flat part of a common hinge attaches to the door, and another attaches to the frame. Little rounded sections on the two parts fit between one another. A pin goes through all of them in a line. Both parts can turn around that pin, so the door can swing without the parts pulling apart sideways. More than one hinge can help carry a tall door.
facts: The small rounded sections that fit around the pin are often called knuckles.

questions.text: How can a spring and oil help some doors close slowly?
Why do scissors have a pin where their two halves cross?
How does a drawbridge raise a piece of road around a turning point?

entries.title: How does a land surveyor measure a place?
entries.answer: A land surveyor measures the positions of points on the ground. Pretend a path is going to cross a hill where no street signs mark the way. The surveyor can record where important features sit and how high they are. Those measurements help a designer know how far apart things are before drawing a plan. Surveyors also look at earlier records when they work out the location of a property boundary.
facts: A hill can change a building plan even when it looks flat on a simple street map.

questions.text: Who brings location measurements together into maps?
What kinds of projects do civil engineers plan?
How does an architect use a plan to organize a building?

entries.title: How does a letter carrier bring many people their mail?
entries.answer: A letter carrier delivers mail to addresses along a route. The carrier needs the right letters and packages for each stop, and may take outgoing mail from places along the way. Some carriers travel mostly on foot, some drive, and some do both. Postal workers in other places have helped sort and move the mail before the carrier sees it. The carrier handles the part that ends at the home or business.
facts: Other postal workers sell stamps or sort mail instead of spending their day on a route.

questions.text: How do sorting machines group mail before a carrier starts?
What can a ZIP Code tell postal workers?
What information helps if a letter needs to go back to the person who sent it?

entries.title: How does a local delivery driver handle many stops?
entries.answer: A local delivery driver might start with many packages going to different places. The order of the stops matters because going back and forth across town wastes time. At each stop, the driver checks which packages belong there and records what happened. Some routes include picking things up as well as dropping them off. A route near a group of shops can be very different from one with homes spread far apart.
facts: A delivery route is a set of stops a worker visits during a trip.

questions.text: How can a person see that a package reached another stop?
How does a letter carrier keep mail for different addresses straight?
Who drives some loads much farther between cities?

entries.title: How does a machinist make a part the exact size it needs to be?
entries.answer: A machinist makes parts that need exact shapes and sizes. A drawing can show whether a part needs a hole, a flat face, or a certain width. The machinist uses machines to shape the material and tools to check its size. A part might look right to the eye and still be a little too large for the place it has to fit. Careful measurements help catch that difference before the part is used.
facts: Some machine tools follow directions stored in a computer.

questions.text: How do workers check whether products match a plan?
Where do carefully made parts go when a product is built?
Who can join metal pieces that need to stay together?

entries.title: How does a mechanical pencil feed out more graphite?
entries.answer: In many mechanical pencils, small jaws grip a thin stick of graphite, the material that leaves the gray mark. Pressing the button shifts the jaws and moves the stick forward a little. The jaws let go briefly as they move back, then grab the stick again to steady it for writing. Several short clicks can bring out more writing material without shaving away any wood.
facts: People often call the writing stick pencil lead, but its dark mark comes from graphite.

questions.text: How does a crank sharpener cut wood away from a pencil?
How does ink get from a ballpoint pen onto paper?
Why does one click extend a pen tip and the next hide it?

entries.title: How does a meteorologist put together a weather forecast?
entries.answer: A meteorologist studies weather and uses clues to forecast what may happen next. A forecaster can look at readings near the ground and at pictures of clouds from space. Computer models also show how the moving air might change over time. A forecast can change when fresh measurements arrive or when different clues suggest different outcomes. The job is about making the best prediction from the information available.
facts: A meteorologist can share both the most likely weather and how uncertain the prediction is.

questions.text: What can a satellite see that one observer on the ground cannot?
How can a boundary between air masses change the weather?
How can someone choose which information to show on a map?

entries.title: How does a reporter find out what happened?
entries.answer: A reporter gathers information about events and explains it to readers, listeners, or viewers. The work can include visiting a place, asking people questions, and reading records. Two people may remember the same event differently, so a reporter may look for another source or a detail that can be checked. After gathering information, a reporter chooses how to tell the story clearly and may work with an editor before it is shared.
facts: A reporter may cover the events of one neighborhood or a subject that matters across many places.

questions.text: Who helps a story become clearer before it is published?
What can a photograph show about an event?
Who can help when people in an interview use different languages?

entries.title: How does a sewing machine join two threads to make a stitch?
entries.answer: A common sewing machine uses one thread from above and another from a small spool below the cloth. The needle carries the upper thread down and then starts back up, leaving a loop. A part under the cloth catches that loop and passes it around the lower spool, linking the two threads. The upper thread pulls tight and the cloth shifts a little before the next stitch.
facts: The small spool under the cloth is called a bobbin.

questions.text: How are yarns combined to make woven cloth?
How can a little loop help two longer strips stay together?
How does a spring clip keep hold of a piece of cloth?

entries.title: How does a zipper join two rows of teeth?
entries.answer: A zipper has two rows of shaped teeth and a part called a slider. When the slider moves one way, it guides the rows together so the teeth catch beside each other. Moving it back guides the teeth apart again. The slider does the work a little at a time as it travels. There is no need to snap the whole row together at once.
facts: Some zippers use metal teeth and others use plastic teeth or a shaped coil.

questions.text: What other fastener sticks because of many tiny catches?
What makes the ends of a staple hold paper together?
How can pulling a piece of tape across an edge cut it?

entries.title: How does an interpreter help two people understand each other?
entries.answer: An interpreter helps people understand a conversation when they use different spoken or signed languages. The interpreter listens or watches closely and gives the message in another language. A translator usually works with written words, where there may be time to check and revise a choice of wording. Both jobs need care with meaning. A joke or a saying that is clear in one language may need a different way of saying it in another.
facts: Interpreting can involve sign language as well as spoken languages.

questions.text: How does a reporter check information from an interview?
Who reads writing carefully before it is published?
How can a reader find books in a library about a particular subject?

entries.title: How quartz helps a clock count seconds
entries.answer: A quartz clock contains a little piece of a mineral that can vibrate. An electronic circuit gives the quartz small pushes so it vibrates at a regular rate. The clock counts those vibrations and turns each set into a step of time. That step can update a display or tell a tiny motor to move hands. Older mechanical clocks can count swings of a much bigger part. The quartz clock uses a much smaller movement.
facts: A common watch crystal vibrates more than thirty thousand times in one second.

questions.text: What movement does a pendulum clock count?
How can measuring many quick changes each second help record a sound?
What turns the hands of some battery-powered clocks?

entries.title: How the Wright brothers learned to fly
entries.answer: Orville and Wilbur Wright tested gliders to learn how to balance an aircraft and turn it. They also made a wind tunnel to try different wing shapes before they built their powered Flyer. In December 1903, near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville flew it first. The brothers took turns through four flights that day. Being able to steer mattered as much as being able to lift off, since an airplane has to stay under control in moving air.
facts: The Wright brothers had worked repairing and making bicycles in Dayton, Ohio.

questions.text: Why were the Wright brothers’ unpowered tests worth doing first?
What did they need a good wing shape to do?
How did the Flyer get a push forward from its engine?

entries.title: What can a librarian help a visitor do?
entries.answer: A librarian helps people find and use information. A visitor might know a story’s title, remember only a character, or be looking for books about wolves without knowing any titles at all. A librarian can use those clues to search and then show the visitor how to do a similar search next time. Librarians may also choose materials for the library or plan activities that help people learn.
facts: Librarians can work in public libraries, schools, or places with special collections.

questions.text: How does a catalog help turn a clue into a book to look for?
How can a call number lead to the right shelf?
How do teachers help children try out ideas?

entries.title: What can an editor notice that a writer misses?
entries.answer: An editor reads writing with fresh eyes and helps prepare it for publication. A writer may know a subject so well that an explanation makes sense in their head while a new reader needs another detail. An editor can spot that gap, suggest a better order, or ask the writer to check a fact. The editor’s work depends on where the writing will appear and who will read it.
facts: Editors can work on things people read on paper, on screens, or in scripts.

questions.text: How does a reporter collect details before writing a story?
Who can notice when a group needs a different example?
How can readers find a published book once a library has it?

entries.title: What do civil engineers make possible?
entries.answer: Civil engineers plan structures and systems that whole communities use. A road project might need a path that follows the land, a way for rain to drain, and enough room for people to cross. A bridge project might need supports that can carry both the bridge and the people using it. Other civil engineers work on water systems. The work starts before a crew begins building and can continue long after a project opens.
facts: Civil engineers work on both new projects and changes to existing ones.

questions.text: Who measures the land before a project starts?
How do inspectors check on bridges that already carry traffic?
Where does rain go after it lands on a street?

entries.title: What do firefighters do between emergency calls?
entries.answer: A firefighter’s work includes being ready for emergencies that are hard to predict. Part of the time at a station may go to checking equipment, practicing as a crew, or learning about the places the team serves. Firefighters respond to fires and may also be called to help with other emergencies. The kinds of work depend on their crew and where it works. A call can arrive while the team is in the middle of something ordinary.
facts: Firefighters may work from a fire station in a neighborhood or from a base in a different setting.

questions.text: Who passes information from a caller to a crew?
Why is there often a hydrant near the street?
Who checks some kinds of work before a building is finished?

entries.title: What do the stripes on a barcode say?
entries.answer: A striped barcode uses dark bars and light gaps of different widths to represent numbers. A scanner can shine light on the stripes and measure the pattern that comes back. The equipment turns that pattern into a number with a known meaning. At a store, the number often identifies the type and size of product so a computer can look up its name or its price. Bottles of the same kind can share the same number.
facts: A store’s own computer normally looks up the price. The stripes do not need to spell out a dollar amount.

questions.text: How can a picture turn patterns of light and dark into stored information?
How can a small number of different symbols represent many numbers?
What changes how much light comes back from a surface?

entries.title: What does a baker do before the bread is ready to sell?
entries.answer: A baker makes foods such as bread and cakes. The work can start with measuring ingredients and mixing them. Dough for some breads needs time to rise, so a baker must plan which batches to start first and when each can go into the oven. A shop may need several kinds ready at once. When something comes out of the oven, a baker may check that it came out as expected before preparing the next batch.
facts: Some bakers begin work before a shop opens so food can be ready when customers arrive.

questions.text: How does yeast help dough puff up?
Who organizes the cooking in a restaurant kitchen?
How can a nearby producer sell goods directly to shoppers?

entries.title: What does a building inspector look for?
entries.answer: A building inspector visits construction projects to check how the work matches rules meant for buildings. An inspector may look at a particular kind of work, such as wiring or plumbing. Some checks happen while parts are still open and easy to see. If the work needs a change, an inspector can tell the builder which part needs attention. Several visits may happen before a project is complete.
facts: Checking work before a wall is closed can reveal details that would later be hidden.

questions.text: Who installs and checks a building’s wiring?
Who puts in pipes and fixtures for water?
Who draws the plans that builders start from?

entries.title: What does a carpenter make on a building site?
entries.answer: A carpenter measures, fits, and joins pieces for buildings. Some carpenters make the framework that holds a wall in place. Others fit doors, stairs, trim, or cabinets that will be visible when the room is finished. A simple part can need careful checking. For example, a door that fits its opening must still have room to move. The carpenter checks the size of the opening and how straight its sides are.
facts: Carpenters work with wood and sometimes with other building materials.

questions.text: Who plans where a room’s doors and walls will go?
How does a hinge help a door turn?
Who fits the glass into a building?

entries.title: What does a cashier check when you buy something?
entries.answer: A cashier helps record what a customer buys and takes payment for it. At some checkouts, a scanner reads a code on each package and the register looks up the item. A cashier may enter information by hand if a code will not scan. The register adds the charges so the customer can see what has been included. After payment, the cashier can hand out a receipt that shows details of the purchase.
facts: Some cashiers also help customers who are returning an item.

questions.text: How does a scanner read the stripes on a barcode?
What can you learn from a receipt?
Who gets products onto the shelves before shoppers arrive?

entries.title: What does a driver do on a long truck trip?
entries.answer: Drivers of heavy trucks carry goods such as food, materials, and finished products. A long trip can begin at a factory, warehouse, or freight yard. The driver needs information about where the load should go and checks that the truck and load are ready. At the other end, the driver works with the people receiving the goods. Another driver might later take smaller loads to nearby shops.
facts: Freight means goods being carried, whether they travel by truck, train, ship, or aircraft.

questions.text: What is different about a route with lots of nearby delivery stops?
How can a truck and freight train both carry the same load on different parts of one trip?
Who plans how goods will move in the first place?

entries.title: What does a head cook do in a busy kitchen?
entries.answer: A head cook or chef helps organize a kitchen so orders can be made and served. Different people might work on different parts of the same meal. The head cook may plan the menu, check that the kitchen has the right supplies, and help decide when each dish should be started. Timing matters because people at the same table may order different foods and still expect to eat together.
facts: A head cook may check dishes before they leave the kitchen.

questions.text: Why does a baker need to plan when batches will be ready?
Who helps keep the items people want ready to find in a shop?
How do shops get food that needs to stay cold along the way?

entries.title: What does a news photographer think about while taking a picture?
entries.answer: A news photographer takes pictures that help show what happened at an event. A wide picture might show how people and objects fit together in one place. A close picture can help a viewer notice an important detail. The photographer has to choose where to stand and when to take the picture. Words beside the image may help explain anything the picture alone cannot show, such as where it was taken.
facts: One photograph does not show everything that happened before or after the moment the camera recorded.

questions.text: What details can a caption add to a photograph?
How can a reporter find facts that a picture cannot show?
Who asks for more details when a published story needs them?

entries.title: What does a plumber do besides fixing a leak?
entries.answer: Plumbers install, check, and fix pipes and the things connected to them. A sink needs a way for clean water to reach its faucet and a different path for used water to drain. Plumbers can work on either side of that system. During construction they follow a plan so pipes reach the right places. During a repair they may have to work out which part is leaking or why water is not moving as expected.
facts: A bathtub, faucet, or toilet connected to pipes is an example of a plumbing fixture.

questions.text: Why is there a curved pipe below many sinks?
How can a water meter measure what passes through a pipe?
How can used water travel uphill on its way to treatment?

entries.title: What does a roofer do to help keep a building dry?
entries.answer: A roofer installs or repairs the covering at the top of a building. A roof can meet a wall, a pipe, or a skylight, so the job includes working around changes in shape. Different roofs use different coverings, from pieces that overlap to large sheets. Roofers may remove damaged material and check the surface below it before putting in a replacement. A well-fitted covering helps water reach the roof’s edges instead of getting indoors.
facts: Roofers work with both steep roofs and roofs that look nearly flat.

questions.text: How do overlapping shingles guide rain down a roof?
Where does water go when it reaches a gutter?
Who fits a glass window in an opening?

entries.title: What does a school bus driver do along a route?
entries.answer: A school bus driver carries pupils between school and stops along a route. The driver follows an assigned set of stops and watches what happens around the bus as people get on and off. Before or after a trip, a driver may check the bus for problems or tell someone about equipment that needs attention. A route can have many small groups of riders, so the driver needs to keep track of the order of stops.
facts: Some school bus drivers also take groups on trips or to activities away from school.

questions.text: How are regular stops used on a public bus route?
What does a driver do on a scheduled public bus route?
Who plans the lessons pupils take after they get to school?

entries.title: What does a school custodian do behind the scenes?
entries.answer: A school custodian helps keep the building clean, orderly, and ready for the people using it. Some work happens while pupils are in other rooms or have gone home. Custodians may clean floors, collect waste, notice when a light has stopped working, or prepare a room for a meeting. They can also report repairs that need a different worker. Their day can change quickly if a busy room needs extra attention.
facts: Custodians may work in schools, offices, shops, or other buildings.

questions.text: Who plans the work students do in a classroom?
Who looks after outdoor spaces around a building?
Where can rubbish go after a collection truck takes it away?

entries.title: What does a wind turbine technician look after?
entries.answer: A wind turbine technician checks and repairs the machines that turn wind into electricity. A turbine can report information about its operation, and technicians can also examine equipment in person. They may look for worn parts or check whether the system responds the way it should. Some work takes place inside a turbine’s tower, high above its base. The machine can make electricity only when its parts are working together.
facts: The generator inside a turbine takes energy from turning parts and changes some of it into electrical energy.

questions.text: Why does wind make a turbine’s blades turn?
Who maintains the lines that bring power toward buildings?
How can electricity from different places reach people who use it?

entries.title: What does an architect do before a building goes up?
entries.answer: An architect turns ideas about a building into plans other people can build from. Imagine a school that needs a new room for music. The architect asks who will use it and what needs to fit inside. The plans show where the walls, doors, and windows go and how people move between rooms. The architect also works with other people, such as engineers, who check whether the parts can carry the loads they will face.
facts: A building plan can show a room from above, as if the roof had been lifted away.

questions.text: Who works out how a bridge or road can carry its loads?
Who checks work at a building site?
Who turns measurements into walls, stairs, and frames?

entries.title: What does an auto mechanic look for when a car has a problem?
entries.answer: An auto mechanic checks how a car or light truck is working and repairs or replaces parts when needed. The job can start with a clue from a driver, such as a noise or a light on the dashboard. A mechanic may look at the car, check stored messages, or test how a part is working. The same garage can also do regular work on a car that has no obvious problem yet.
facts: The same symptom can have more than one cause, so mechanics check evidence before choosing a repair.

entries.title: What does an electrician do in a building?
entries.answer: An electrician installs, checks, and repairs electrical systems. In a new room, a plan might call for several lights, switches, and places to plug in equipment. Wires connect those parts to the building’s electrical supply. On a repair job, an electrician may check which part of the system is causing a problem. From the room, people usually see the switches and lights, while much of the work stays out of sight inside walls or above ceilings.
facts: A circuit is a path through which electric current can flow.

entries.title: What does an elementary school teacher do when a class is learning?
entries.answer: An elementary school teacher plans ways to help children learn. The teacher might explain an idea, let pupils try it, then look at their work to see whether another explanation would help. Two children may understand the same idea after different examples. Teachers also choose materials, organize classroom time, and talk with other adults about how to support children. Planning and checking work happen outside lessons as well as during them.
facts: One classroom teacher may teach several subjects in the course of a day.

entries.title: What happens at the other end of a call for emergency help?
entries.answer: Workers at an emergency call center gather information and get it to the right responders. The person taking the call may ask which place needs help and what is happening there. Workers may also keep track of teams that are already out so new information reaches the right people. Some centers divide call taking and sending crews between different workers. The callers, call center, and people at the scene are each in a different place.
facts: Dispatchers may communicate with responding crews by radio or computer.

entries.title: What made a daguerreotype different from a modern print?
entries.answer: A daguerreotype is an early type of photograph. The image sits on a thin coat of silver over a copper plate. Tilt the plate in the light and some parts can look lighter or darker as the shiny surface reflects what is around it. Each plate held a single original image. If someone wanted another picture, the plate could not simply be used to print a stack of matching copies on paper.
facts: The process was announced in France in 1839.

entries.title: What makes hook-and-loop fasteners stick together?
entries.answer: One side of a hook-and-loop fastener has many tiny hooks. The soft side has small loops. When you press the two sides together, some hooks catch loops and hold the strips close. Peeling from one end pulls the hooks free a few at a time, which is easier than trying to pull the whole strip apart at once. The same fastener can then close again.
facts: The soft and rough sides can both collect lint or bits of thread.

entries.title: What turns inside a crank pencil sharpener?
entries.answer: A crank pencil sharpener has small cutters inside that roll around the tip of the pencil when you turn the handle. The cutters shave away thin pieces of wood and shape the dark part in the middle into a point. The pencil can stay still in the opening while the cutters move. The little chips fall into a tray so they don’t cover the desk.
facts: Some hand sharpeners use one fixed blade and ask you to turn the pencil instead.

entries.title: Who checks whether the things a factory makes are right?
entries.answer: A quality control inspector checks parts or finished products against a plan. One piece may need to be a certain length. Another may need a test to see whether it works as expected. The inspector can look for damage, measure a part, or use special equipment to find a problem that is hard to see. The results help a factory find trouble before more of the same pieces are made.
facts: Different products need different kinds of checks, even in the same factory.

entries.title: Who decides how products should get from one place to another?
entries.answer: People who work in logistics make plans for moving and storing things. If a shop needs boxes by Friday, someone has to find out where the boxes are, how much space they take, and which trip can get them there. A plan that works for books might not suit ice cream, which needs cold storage. Logistics workers watch for delays and can pass updates to the people who are waiting.
facts: Moving things quickly is only one goal. Deliveries also need to arrive in the right place and in useful condition.

entries.title: Who designs the outdoor parts of a park?
entries.answer: A landscape architect plans outdoor places such as parks, plazas, and schoolyards. The job can include deciding where paths go, which parts stay open for play, and where trees can give shade. The designer also thinks about water after rain and how people with different ways of moving can reach the same places. A good plan joins the parts together so they can work as one outdoor space.
facts: Landscape architects may plan gardens and paths around buildings as well as separate parks.

entries.title: Who helps keep a grocery store’s shelves filled?
entries.answer: A grocery stock worker moves products from storage to the places where shoppers look for them. When several boxes look alike, the worker needs to check which exact product belongs in each space. Shelves may be filled while the store is quiet or as things run out during the day. Some jobs also involve checking what has arrived and noticing which products are running low. Labels help workers keep different sizes and kinds separated.
facts: A worker may bring goods from the back room even when a shelf at the front looks empty.

entries.title: Who helps keep an airplane’s equipment working?
entries.answer: Aircraft mechanics inspect, maintain, and repair equipment used on aircraft. An airplane depends on many parts working together, so checks include written instructions and records of what was done. One airplane may need parts checked at planned times. Another may need work after a crew reports a problem. A mechanic can examine the equipment, replace a part if needed, and record the result so later workers can follow the airplane’s work history.
facts: Some aircraft technicians work mainly on the electronic equipment in a plane.

entries.title: Who keeps the grounds around a park or school ready to use?
entries.answer: Groundskeepers care for outdoor places people use. Their tasks depend on the place. A school might need paths cleared and the edge of a playing field trimmed. A park might need young trees watered or a rough area put back in good condition. The work changes with the seasons. Before a big event, a groundskeeper may check parts that usually need less attention so people can get around easily.
facts: Watering a new plant and caring for one that is established can be different jobs.

entries.title: Who looks after elevators and escalators?
entries.answer: Elevator and escalator technicians install or care for machines that move people between levels. In a new building they fit equipment into the planned space. In a building already in use they may check parts, notice wear, or follow up on a problem someone reports. A smooth trip depends on more than a motor. Doors, controls, and moving parts have to work together, and technicians check the whole system.
facts: Some technicians also work on moving walkways like the ones found in large airports.

entries.title: Who looks after the wires that carry power through a town?
entries.answer: Power line workers install and repair the cables that bring electricity from the grid toward buildings. Some lines pass above streets, while other lines run underground. A crew may be working on a new route or finding which part of a line needs repair after a storm. The work may involve reaching places that are high above the ground or far from a road. The crew handles special equipment for the job.
facts: Power lines carry electricity between many places even when buildings use different amounts at different times.

entries.title: Who organizes games and activities at a recreation center?
entries.answer: A recreation worker helps people use their free time for things such as games, crafts, and sports. Planning might include choosing an activity, collecting materials, and deciding how to share a room among groups. A good organizer thinks about the people who will be there. A game for children who have played together all year may need a different start from one for children meeting for the first time.
facts: Recreation workers may run programs at camps, parks, and community centers.

questions.text: How can someone choose a different example for a group that needs it?

entries.title: Who puts the glass into a building?
entries.answer: A worker called a glazier fits glass into openings and fixtures. Glaziers might put in a shop window, a glass door, or a window in a roof. They need to check the opening and the glass so the pieces match. Some jobs involve replacing a pane that was already there. Others involve several panels in a large wall. In each case the surrounding frame helps keep the glass in its place.
facts: A skylight is a window that lets light in through a roof.

entries.title: Who watches over the machines that clean a town’s water?
entries.answer: A water plant operator pays attention to the machines and tests that are part of treating water. At a drinking water plant, the goal is to prepare water before it travels through pipes to the people using it. At a wastewater plant, the work happens after water has been used. Operators watch readings, check equipment, and respond when something changes. They keep records so the next person on duty knows what has happened.
facts: A water plant may need someone to monitor its work even when most of the town is asleep.

entries.title: Who works on an ambulance crew?
entries.answer: Emergency medical technicians and paramedics are trained workers who can care for people at an emergency. An ambulance crew may need to find out what happened, bring equipment from the ambulance, and decide how to move someone who needs further care. If the crew takes someone to a medical center, its members can pass important information to the people who will help next. The crew’s exact duties depend on training and the place where it works.
facts: EMT is short for emergency medical technician.

entries.title: Why can a bottle opener lift a cap with a small push?
entries.answer: A metal crown cap has bent edges that grip the bottle’s rim. A bottle opener can slip an edge under one side of the cap while another part of the opener rests against it. When the handle moves, the opener turns around its resting point and lifts part of the cap. The bend frees enough of the edge for the cap to come away.
facts: A crown cap is named for its ring of small ridges around the edge.

entries.title: Why do some factories and building crews need welders?
entries.answer: A welder joins metal parts so they can work as a larger piece. A factory may need several pieces joined for a frame. A repair crew may need to fix a joint on a machine that is already in use. The welder checks what the drawing calls for and prepares to join the right pieces in the right place. Other parts of the job can include looking at the finished joint and keeping track of work that is complete.
facts: Welders can work indoors in factories or outdoors on jobs such as bridge construction.

entries.title: Why do the ends of a staple bend under the paper?
entries.answer: When you press a stapler, a flat piece pushes one staple down through the paper. Its two legs meet small grooves in a hard plate underneath. These grooves guide the legs inward as they bend. The bent metal now sits across the underside of the pages, with the top of the staple above them. The pages stay together because the bent legs are in the way.
facts: The plate under the staple is called an anvil, a name also used for a support people hammer metal against.

entries.title: Why does a ballpoint pen have a tiny ball?
entries.answer: The end of a ballpoint pen holds a tiny ball that can roll but cannot fall out. Inside the pen, ink wets the inner side of the ball. As the tip moves across paper, the ball rolls. That brings a fresh bit of ink from inside the pen to its outside, where it leaves a mark. The writer supplies the motion by moving the tip.
facts: Some pens made for space use gas pressure to keep ink moving toward the ball.

entries.title: Why does a tape dispenser have little teeth?
entries.answer: A tape dispenser lets the roll turn as you pull tape away from it. The cutting edge has a row of small points. When tape presses against the points, each tip puts force on a very small area and starts a little cut. As the tape pulls against the edge, those cuts meet. The tape comes off the roll at the length you pulled.
facts: Some dispensers have a flat spot that holds the loose end until the next use.

entries.title: Why does one pen click extend the tip and the next hide it?
entries.answer: A retractable pen has a moving ink tube, a spring, and a small guide inside the case. In one design, a part catches on a raised step in the guide and holds the pen tip out. The next press moves the part to another place in the guide. The spring can then pull or push the tip back inside, depending on how the pieces are arranged.
facts: The shaped guide in many moving devices is called a cam.

entries.title: Why might one factory worker make only one part of a toy?
entries.answer: An assembly worker fits parts together to help make a product. Imagine a toy truck with an axle, wheels, and a body. One worker could fit pieces at one stop, while another worker adds a different part later. At some factories, workers and machines share the steps. Each finished object depends on parts arriving in useful order and fitting together. Some teams build a whole object at one work area instead.
facts: Assemblers may put together tiny electronic devices or very large objects such as equipment.
